cases.cat: Misleading presentation of study data (real-world evidence / comparative)
cases.heading: False or Misleading Benefit Presentation
cases.claim: “In a Real-World Study with nearly 11,000 patients Pegfilgrastim PFS resulted in a significantly higher risk of FN vs. Onpro®” | “Across all cycles of chemotherapy, the incidence of FN associated with prefilled syringe (PFS) was 1.7% (n = 455) vs 1.3% (n = 126) for Neulasta® Onpro®” | “31%* *p = 0.01” | “With PFS, FN incidence increased by 31% vs Onpro®”
cases.context: Retrospective claims study; unvalidated FN algorithm; no control for selection bias; absolute difference 0.4%; limitations in frames 7-8 do not mitigate.
cases.rationale: Study design limitations preclude comparative conclusions; reporting p-value is misleading; relative risk emphasized over small absolute difference.
cases.check: Do comparative effectiveness claims rest on retrospective/RWE data with unvalidated outcome definitions or uncontrolled confounding? Is relative risk emphasized over absolute difference?

cases.heading: False or Misleading Benefit Presentation
cases.claim: “Pegfilgrastim PFS” presented as comparator vs “Neulasta Onpro” and “Onpro”
cases.context: Use of nonproprietary name for PFS arm vs proprietary name for OBI; frame six statement that both arms were Neulasta was less prominent.
cases.rationale: Could lead HCPs to conclude biosimilar pegfilgrastim (PFS-only) is less effective than Neulasta Onpro.
cases.check: Does naming of comparator arms (generic vs brand) imply inferiority of competitor/biosimilar products not studied?
